title: Control flow
description: if, while, for, and match in Java

exercises.title: If Statement
exercises.description: Declare age = 20. If age >= 18, System.out.println Adult. Otherwise System.out.println Minor.

exercises.title: For Loop
exercises.description: Use a for loop to System.out.println numbers 1 through 5.
hints: Use a classic `for (int i = 1; i <= 5; i++)` and `System.out.println(i);`.

exercises.title: Switch Statement
exercises.description: Declare day = 2. Use a switch statement to System.out.println the day name: 1=Monday, 2=Tuesday, 3=Wednesday, default=Unknown.
hints: Use `switch (day)` with `case` labels and `break;` (or a `switch` expression with arrows in Java 14+).

exercises.title: For-Range Loop
exercises.description: Create a slice colors = int[] {"red", "green", "blue"}. Use for ... in to System.out.println each color on its own line.
hints: Create `String[] colors = {"red", "green", "blue"};` and a enhanced `for (String color : colors)` loop.
Print each color on its own line.

exercises.title: Else If Chain
exercises.description: Declare score = 85. Print the grade: 90+ = A, 80+ = B, 70+ = C, 60+ = D, below 60 = F.
hints: Chain conditions with `if / else if` or a nested conditional expression as in the solution.
For score `85`, the result must be `B`.

exercises.title: For Loop with Break
exercises.description: Use a for loop to count from 1 upward. When i reaches 5, break out of the loop. Print each number before the break.
hints: Print `1` through `4` — a `for (int i = 1; i < 5; i++)` matches the reference solution.
Alternatively use `break` once `i == 5` in an infinite `for (;;)` loop.

exercises.title: Continue Statement
exercises.description: Use a for loop to System.out.println numbers 1 to 10, but skip System.out.printlning even numbers using continue.
hints: Print odd numbers only, one per line.
